default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-888.title: Narrowest-range bar break
E-888.hypothesis: A bar with the smallest range of the last n bars marks compression; the next close beyond its extreme releases stored orders in that direction.

E-889.title: Return acceleration follow
E-889.hypothesis: A move that is both large for the instrument and more than twice as fast as the previous equal window shows forced flow still arriving; follow it.

E-890.title: Higher-high higher-low run
E-890.hypothesis: Several bars in a row that each raise both high and low (or lower both) show one-sided participation that has not met resistance; follow the onset.

E-891.title: Volume spike confirmation follow
E-891.hypothesis: After a bar with volume far above normal, a next close beyond the spike bar's close confirms the aggressor won; follow.

E-892.title: Late-session trend-side new extreme
E-892.hypothesis: In the final hour, fresh extremes in the direction of the day's drift come from institutions rebalancing into the close; follow.

E-893.title: Prior clock-hour range break
E-893.hypothesis: The previous clock hour's high and low are levels watched by intraday traders; a close beyond them triggers stops and follow-through.

E-894.title: Rising-volume directional run
E-894.hypothesis: Consecutive bars of the same colour each on more volume than the last show growing commitment, not exhaustion; follow the onset.

E-895.title: Day-displacement sigma cross follow
E-895.hypothesis: When the day's move from the open exceeds a typical same-time move by k times, the day is trending and late participants chase it.

E-896.title: Extreme recency tilt follow
E-896.hypothesis: If the session low is set much more recently than the session high, sellers gave up last; a close above a short EMA follows that tilt (and the reverse).

E-897.title: Equity-open window range shock follow
E-897.hypothesis: Between 10:30 and 12:00 the US cash open brings foreign flow; a bar with a range far above normal and a strong close shows it, and the move continues.
